ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of each general partner, each 25%+ limited-partner beneficial owner, and each authorized signatory against the consolidated Canadian sanctions lists administered by Global Affairs Canada under the United Nations Act, the Special Economic Measures Act, and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act; the Consolidated United Nations Security Council Sanctions List; the OFAC SDN List and Sectoral Sanctions Identifications given USD clearing through PayPal and Wise; and FINTRAC domestic PEP and Heads of International Organizations determinations under PCMLTFA ss. 9.3, 9.4 and 12-12.1. Screening must be conducted prior to registration, repeated at onboarding of each new partner, and refreshed on every anniversary; any positive hit requires enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, and a written clearance memorandum issued by the designated AML compliance officer before admission to the partnership.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – online portal, https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11, the registered business name must be in French; a name in another language is admissible only where a French version is of at least equal prominence or the Office québécois de la langue française (OQLF) has granted an exception; transliteration into Latin script must respect the French spelling and punctuation norms; all partnership documentation, contracts, and platform-facing Quebec communications must be available in French; the name may not falsely suggest a status other than a limited partnership, so only 'S.E.C.' or 'L.P.' or 'société en commandite' designations are permitted without misleading words such as 'Inc.', 'Corporation', 'LLC', or 'Ltd.'.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank / Banque / Banking (requires federal or provincial banking license)
Insurance / Assurance (requires AMF or OSFI authorization)
Montréal (when used in a manner implying public authority)
Ingénieur / Avocat / Notaire / Comptable professionnel agréé (regulated professional titles requiring competent-order authorization)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A REQ name reservation is valid for 60 days and may be extended administratively for one additional 60-day period upon application to the Registraire, provided the proposed name is unchanged and still available. Upon rejection, the applicant may: (1) request a written statement of reasons from the Registraire within 10 days; (2) file a demande de révision (administrative review) with the Registraire within 30 days of the refusal; (3) if the review is unsuccessful, file an originating application in the Civil Division of the Court of Québec within 60 days of the review decision; and (4) if the refusal arises solely from insufficiency of the French-language form, submit a linguistic approval or exception application to the Office québécois de la langue française prior to re-pre-clearance. Should a third party oppose the name on confusion grounds, the applicant may either obtain the third party's written consent or seek a civil remedy for approval of a distinguishing element under the Court's statutory jurisdiction.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for this industry only where a licensed Quebec registered agent or law firm maintains a physical street address in the province and agrees to receive service of process and forward correspondence; a postal-only or mail-forwarding virtual office or PO Box does not satisfy the establishment-address requirement of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, s. 17 and art. 2250 CCQ; no physical office, employees, or dedicated assets in Quebec are statutorily required for a consumer-panel SaaS market-research platform.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec, arts. 2236–2252 (limited partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, ss. 38–45 (registration of enterprises); no separate Companies Act applies to limited partnerships in Quebec.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation (Declaration of Registration) filed in the Registraire des entreprises du Québec central registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital or statutory escrow requirement applies to a Quebec limited partnership. Limited partners must, however, contribute the capital agreed in the partnership agreement to enjoy limited liability under Civil Code of Québec art. 2240; contributions may be held in escrow only if the partnership agreement imposes that condition.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the Limited Partnership is hereby formed under the Civil Code of Québec and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. Capital Contributions: The General Partner and the limited partners shall subscribe for partnership interests as set out in the executed limited partnership agreement, and contributions are effective upon deposit in the partnership bank account. Registered Office: The registered office is fixed at the address stated in the Declaration of Registration. Officers and Agent: The General Partner is appointed to manage the partnership; the Chief Executive Officer and Corporate Secretary are authorized to file all registry declarations, open bank and payment accounts, engage PayPal Mass Payout and Wise, obtain tax numbers, and execute incidental documents. This resolution binds the partnership.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Verify Business Name and Confirm Structural Eligibility
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – online business name research service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the REQ 'Recherche d'un nom' portal to verify availability of the proposed partnership name, e.g. 'Consumer Panel Survey Platform S.E.C.' or 'Consumer Panel Survey Platform Limited Partnership'. Confirm that the name file does not conflict with existing trademarks or corporate names. If a higher degree of certainty is required, request a REQ name analysis (analyse de nom) prior to registration.
required_dossiers: Proposed partnership name and alternative names
Brief statement of activities (ISIC 7320 / NAICS 541910)
General partner's identity document and contact details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, amend the name and resubmit; if the specific name is already registered, select an acceptable available alternative and file a corrected Declaration of Registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute the Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Parties' legal counsel; no government filing required for the internal agreement itself
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare a partnership agreement under Civil Code of Québec arts. 2236–2252 covering identity and capital contribution of each limited partner, profit-sharing formula, management authority of the general partner, withdrawal and transfer rights, dispute resolution, and dissolution events. The original agreement need not be notarized, but each partner's signature must be witnessed. A French or English version is acceptable for REQ filing; if the entity will transact in English with non-residents, maintain a certified English version in the corporate records.
required_dossiers: Limited partnership agreement signed by all general and limited partners
Capital contribution schedule or bank deposit receipt
Identification documents and residential/professional addresses of partners
Declaration of designated general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a partner signs under defective authority or the agreement contains ambiguous capital clauses, cure by obtaining re-execution or a written rectification signed by all partners before filing the Declaration of Registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Declaration of Registration with the Quebec Enterprise Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – online service 'Espace REQ'
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the REQ online portal and submit the Déclaration d'immatriculation for the limited partnership (société en commandite). Provide the registered office address, general partner name and address, and the partnership's principal activity. Pay the required filing fee using an accepted payment method. The registration becomes effective on the timestamp of REQ's acceptance, and a Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) is issued. A notarized power of attorney is required only where the filing agent is not one of the partners and acts under representation.
required_dossiers: Completed Declaration of Registration form (REQ e-form)
Executed limited partnership agreement
Name analysis certificate or name waiver if obtained
Proof of registered office address in Quebec
Identification of the general partner and each limited partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ issues a query or refusal, respond within the time stated in the notice, provide the missing information, and file an amended declaration (déclaration modificative) to correct any discrepancies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Federal and Quebec Tax Accounts and Business Numbers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: With the NEQ, register the partnership with the CRA for a Business Number (BN) and GST/HST account if taxable sales exceed the registration threshold or if voluntary registration is advisable for input tax credits. Register with Revenu Québec for a Quebec Business Number and QST account. Since the entity is a limited partnership, the general partner manages filings for the collective; set up employer accounts only if employees will be hired. Use the CRA Business Registration Online portal and Revenu Québec's 'Mon dossier d'entreprise'.
required_dossiers: NEQ registration certificate
Limited partnership agreement
General partner's social insurance number or corporate identification
Bank confirmation of partnership account
Projected gross revenue statement for threshold assessment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA and Revenu Québec data do not reconcile, file an adjustment to the registrant particulars with the entity that returned the notice and verify that the NEQ, BN, and QST numbers are cross-referenced; apply for late registration relief if a deadline was missed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Canadian Partnership Bank Account and Activate Payment Rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Schedule I Canadian chartered bank or federally regulated credit union (institution of general partner's choice)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a dedicated partnership bank account at a Canadian bank using the NEQ certificate and the executed partnership agreement. Provide the general partner's personal or corporate identification and a list of authorized signing officers. Once the account is open, use the business data and bank details to complete PayPal Mass Payout applicant verification and Wise business onboarding for mass cross-border survey-incentive payments. Maintain a single bank account to preserve partnership capital records.
required_dossiers: Quebec enterprise registration certificate (NEQ)
Executed limited partnership agreement
Certificate of incumbency listing authorized signatories
General partner's government-issued photo ID and proof of address
Business plan or anticipated payment flow description for AML review
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or payment provider rejects the application, provide updated corrected formation documents, obtain a reference letter from counsel, or apply to a secondary bank; for payment rails, escalate to PayPal/Wise compliance after verifying that the registered legal name and address match exactly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Satisfy Municipal Business Licensing and Leased Premises Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Québec municipality where the registered office is located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Check the local municipal by-law for any office-use business licence. Although ISIC 7320 market research and survey platforms do not require a provincial occupational licence, a municipal 'permis d'exploitation' or zoning approval may be required if commercial premises are used. Obtain from the landlord the building occupancy permit and fire safety attestation for the leased office. Display the NEQ in the registered office if required by the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.
required_dossiers: Commercial lease or registered office consent form
Landlord's occupancy certificate
Municipal business licence application (if applicable)
NEQ certificate
Commercial general liability insurance certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality issues a zoning or licensing refusal, apply for a minor variance or request confirmation that professional office use is a permitted use; otherwise relocate the registered office and amend the REQ declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establish Corporate Governance and Statutory Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General partner, partnership secretary, and legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first meeting of the general partner and adopt the written resolution approving the limited partnership agreement, registered office, capital subscriptions, and officers. Maintain a register of partners and capital accounts, minutes of partner decisions, tax election records, and data protection compliance documentation under Quebec's private sector privacy law. Document the authorization to use PayPal Mass Payout and Wise for cross-border consumer panel rewards.
required_dossiers: Signed first resolution of the general partner
Register of partnership units or capital contributions
Partner notification and consent forms
Data privacy policy and PIPEDA/P-39.1 compliance checklist
Authorized signatory list for payment accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a governance record is defective or omitted, cure by adopting a subsequent written resolution confirming ratification, amending the minute book, and filing any necessary rectification with REQ and tax authorities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – no industrial licensing board has jurisdiction over ISIC 7320/NAICS 541910 consumer polling and market research platform services; office-based activity only.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None – statutory provincial occupation licensing is not required for a market research SaaS platform; municipal occupancy permits and business licences may apply to physical premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no full EIA, environmental registration, or attestation required because the activity is an office-based service business with no industrial discharges, no fixed combustion equipment, and no physical pollutant emissions.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No Quebec environmental discharge standards apply to pure consumer polling software operations. Office waste must be disposed of through municipal commercial waste collection. If future on-premise data centres, call centres with diesel backup, or physical testing facilities are added, a new environmental compliance assessment under the Environment Quality Act (CQLR c Q-2) will be required for standby generator exhaust, wastewater, and electronic waste handling.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: obtain from the building owner the fire safety attestation and ensure compliance with the Quebec Fire Safety Code (CQLR c B-1.1, r. 8), including maintained extinguishers, unobstructed exits, emergency lighting, and an evacuation plan for the office floor. Structural load inspection: rely on the landlord's building occupancy certificate; the office lease must confirm that ordinary office loading is structurally permitted. Occupational clearance: no CNESST-specific clearance certificate is required for a low-risk office environment, but the employer must register with CNESST if employees are hired, implement a basic health and safety orientation, provide ergonomic equipment, and keep a first-aid kit in accordance with CNESST standards.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA, Agence du revenu du Canada) via Business Registration Online (BRO) and My Business Account portal; Revenu Québec via Mon dossier d'entreprise / CLIC portal; Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) for the compulsory Quebec enterprise number (NEQ).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Appoint the Canadian general partner and file the limited partnership declaration with REQ under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises to obtain the NEQ. 2) Register the partnership for a federal Business Number (BN) through CRA Business Registration Online or Form RC1, selecting the GST/HST program account (RT) and payroll account (RC) if applicable; the BN is issued to the partnership as a separate person for GST/HST purposes. 3) Register with Revenu Québec for the QST using the NEQ, obtaining a 10-digit QST registration number (TQ account); use the single-window registration or Form LM-1-V. 4) File the federal partnership information return (T5013) and the Quebec partnership return (TP-600) with RL-15 slips when a corporate or non-resident partner exists or partnership gross revenue exceeds CAD 2,000,000. 5) Enroll in CRA My Business Account and Revenu Québec CLIC for electronic filing, assessments, and audit correspondence. Typical turnaround is 24–72 hours for BN and QST issuance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible: the limited partnership is fiscally transparent for income tax under ITA section 96, with each partner reporting its allocable share directly; no entity-level income tax. For GST/HST and QST, the partnership is a separate person under ETA section 177(1) and is the registrant/collector on taxable supplies. Territorial scope: income allocated to Canadian-resident partners is fully subject to Canadian and Quebec tax; income allocated to non-resident partners from active Canadian-source service business is taxed through a non-resident Part I filing (T1159) and is not subject to Part XIII withholding, unless the allocation represents passive payments such as management fees. No tax-exempt zone applies. Quebec may impose the health services fund (FSS) payroll tax if the partnership employs Quebec personnel.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not have a federal check-the-box regime; entity classification is statutory. Relevant elections for a Quebec limited partnership: (a) voluntary GST/HST registration by a small supplier under ETA section 240 and the corresponding QST registration; (b) election under ETA section 156 to deem supplies between closely related registrants to be for nil consideration, mirrored in QSTA provisions for Quebec; (c) partnership registration and deemed-person rules under ETA section 177 (with QSTA equivalent) permitting the partnership itself to register and file rather than the general partner; (d) income tax rollover elections under ITA section 97(2) for transfer of property to the partnership on a tax-deferred basis; (e) hybrid mismatch rules in ITA sections 18.2–18.6 may disallow deductions on payments where the counterparty is a hybrid entity; a US member may file Form 8832 for US check-the-box purposes, but that election has no direct Canadian tax consequence.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal value-added tax at 5%) plus QST (Quebec Sales Tax at 9.975% computed on the GST-inclusive price; combined effective compound rate 15.47375%; combined headline statutory sum 14.975%). Standard-rated supplies of consumer panel survey and market research services; zero-rated exports to non-residents.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold under ETA section 148(1); identical CAD 30,000 threshold applies for QST under the Quebec Sales Tax Act; tested on taxable supplies made in a single calendar quarter and in the preceding four calendar quarters.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, API government stamping, or QR-code fiscal invoice regime exists in Canada. The Pan-Canadian PEPPOL e-invoicing standard is voluntary; CRA and Revenu Québec accept EDI and XML e-invoices. Suppliers must retain issue records and electronically file information returns (T4A and RL-1/RL-15) when applicable to panelist incentive payments exceeding regulatory slip thresholds; zero-rated export invoices must be coded as such with supporting documentation retained.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of market research, polling, and data analytics services to non-residents qualify for 0% GST/HST under Part V, Schedule VI, ETA, section 7, and for 0% QST under Schedule III, QSTA, section 30, provided the service is not supplied to an individual present in Canada and does not relate to real property situated in Canada, tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time of performance, or intangible personal property exploited principally in Canada. The supplier must maintain contemporaneous evidence of the non-resident status of the recipient and of offshore service delivery/consumption.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA Form B13A) plus Bill of Lading or air waybill, required only where tangible survey materials or incentive goods are shipped from Canada; pure service exports to non-residents require no customs export declaration.

Export commercial invoice and master services agreement evidencing supply to a non-resident counterparty, supported by platform IP-location logs and user-metadata records demonstrating consumption outside Canada, together with a non-resident status file (W-8BEN-E for US clients, foreign certificate of incorporation, or tax residency certificate).

Inward remittance confirmation, SWIFT/Wise transaction record, or PayPal Mass Payout settlement ledger proving receipt of funds from the foreign payer within the 180-day settlement covenant, plus partnership books and T5013/RL-15 allocation schedules substantiating the zero-rated revenue.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess zero-rating claims within the normal four-year reassessment window under ETA section 298 (extended to eight years for misrepresentation or non-resident-related cases; QSTA section 991 mirrors). If contemporaneous export documentation is inadequate, the full 5% GST and 9.975% QST are retrospectively clawed back to the supply date with associated input tax credit disallowances, prescribed quarterly interest, and penalties: ETA section 280 false statement penalty of the greater of CAD 250 and 5% of the related tax; ETA section 285 gross negligence penalty of 25% of the tax sought to be avoided; QSTA equivalent penalties under sections 991–993; and Criminal Code section 380 fraud liability (imprisonment up to 14 years) where the zero-rating claim is made with intent to deceive.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); foreign exchange administration is exercised under the Currency Act and the Minister of Finance mandate, with operational compliance oversight by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility. There are no general exchange controls, no surrender requirements for export proceeds, and no restrictions on profit remittance for non-resident partners of a Quebec Limited Partnership. Distribution payments to foreign partners are freely transferable abroad, subject to Part XIII non-resident withholding tax (typically 15% unless reduced by tax treaty) and to reporting of cross-border currency movements exceeding CAD 10,000 under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canadian law does not mandate conversion, surrender, or repatriation of export/foreign-currency proceeds. However, survey platform payments received from non-resident clients that are booked as export revenue may be subject to mandatory reporting under the Statistics Act for Balance of Payments compilation, and any cross-border movement of physical currency, bearer instruments, or monetary instruments over CAD 10,000 must be reported to the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) and FINTRAC.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility. Wise (formerly TransferWise) Canada and PayPal Canada are registered Money Services Businesses (MSBs) under FINTRAC, not banks or Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) in the Canadian legal framework. They may be used as complementary payment rails for cross-border consumer panel incentives, mass payouts, and low-value disbursements, but they cannot serve as the sole operating bank for the limited partnership. Legal constraints: no deposit-taking authority; customer funds must be held in segregated trust accounts at a Canadian FDIC-insured bank; unregistered offshore EMIs are prohibited from soliciting Canadian clients and are subject to enforcement by FINTRAC and provincial securities regulators.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under the PCMLTFA and FINTRAC Guidance (including the 2023 updates), a bank may open an account for a Canadian limited partnership without a mandatory physical interview of general partners if it performs remote identification using encrypted copies of government-issued IDs, independent corroboration from registry records (Quebec Enterprise Registrar – REQ), and a videoconference with a designated senior officer. In practice, Canadian Schedule I banks will usually require a Canadian-registered address, the appointment of an authorized signatory, and may demand a physical or virtual appointment for heightened-risk, cross-border structures. Remote onboarding is permitted; the bank must evidence reasonable measures to verify the identity of each controlling partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Limited partnership structure with non-resident limited partners and a foreign general partner creates beneficial-ownership opacity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide notarized Partnership Agreement, certified register of partners with full legal name/DOB/residence, corporate registry extracts from Quebec REQ and foreign jurisdictions; a clear organizational chart; and a declaration of ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) for each partner holding ≥10% interest.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital contribution arrives from a third-party (non-partner) jurisdiction (e.g., from foreign parent or technology venture fund) and appears unrelated to the business plan
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit executed capital contribution agreement, bank source-of-funds letter from originating institution, audited or accountant-reviewed financial statements of the contributor, evidence of tax identification number, and a sworn source-of-wealth statement explaining funds originated from lawful commercial activities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No physical office or employee presence in Canada; no Canadian-director representation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the LP's registered business address agreement (e.g., virtual office from a Quebec chartered professional accountant), service plan with Canadian legal counsel, board resolution appointing a Canadian financial services provider as agent for service of process, and an operational commitment letter showing periodic Canada-based compliance visits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency cross-border micro-payments to consumer panel participants may be flagged as layering or unlicensed money remittance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a detailed AML program manual, FINTRAC MSB registration confirmation (if applicable), policies for customer due diligence (CDD) on panelists, transactional monitoring systems, history or projected flows reconciled to the survey platform business plan, and evidence of contractual payments for services rendered.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of clear economic purpose for maintaining a Quebec LP used only for consumer panel data collection
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare a commercial substance memorandum explaining the use of Quebec local marketing partners, data-residency requirements, employee/contractor roster, billing and collection workflows, and a forecast of Canada-source revenues versus outbound payments; attach the ISIC 7320 market-research service agreement and data-processing addendum.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocol via SWIFT MT103 from a foreign parent or investor. Originator must include: full legal name of remitter, account number, correspondent bank routing (intermediary if necessary), ISO purpose code reflecting 'capital contribution / equity injection' (SWIFT Category B, e.g., AT01 or ERCL), and in field 70 (Remittance Information) must state 'Capital contribution – CA_LP – Quebec Enterprise Registry #[REQ number]'. Beneficiary bank (Canada Schedule I) must receive first a signed KYC resolution, certified LP agreement, and fund-source attestation. For transfers exceeding CAD 10,000 in equivalent cross-border currency or cash, the bank will report the transaction to FINTRAC. No prior central-bank approval is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements include (i) SWIFT MT103/MT202 coverage via correspondent banks for direct vendor payments; (ii) Commercial Documentary Letters of Credit (L/C), particularly through Canadian banks with foreign confirming bank branches, for high-value survey-panel recruitment or research outsourcing; and (iii) Payments Canada’s Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) for domestic CAD disbursements, converted to cross-border SWIFT payments. All outbound payments must be screened against OFAC/UN sanctions lists; for amounts above CAD 10,000, FINTRAC's electronic reporting obligations apply. The LP must retain a transaction-level audit trail for profit remittances to non-resident partners.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Over-the-counter (OTC) deliverable currency forwards (CAD/USD) under ISDA 1992/2002 CSA
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing CAD/USD or CAD/EUR for speculative cross-border receivables exposure
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) between CAD and USD or other G7 currencies for funding and balance-sheet hedging
Plain-vanilla foreign exchange options (calls/puts) on CAD pairs, sold and purchased under a Canadian Securities Administrator exemptive relief for non-dealer corporate hedgers

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) to the Registraire des entreprises du Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For registration anniversaries from January 1 through April 30: due June 15. For anniversaries from May 1 through December 31: due no later than the last day of the month preceding the registration anniversary.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of CAD 25 (approx. USD 19) under the enterprise registration regulations; failure to file for two consecutive years triggers administrative strike-off of the LP registration; after strike-off the entity cannot lawfully operate or assert limited partnership status against third parties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Partnership Information Return (T5013) and partner allocation slips
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the partnership's fiscal period end. For a calendar-year fiscal period ending December 31, the return is due by May 31 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CRA late-filing penalties under s. 162(3) of the Income Tax Act, starting at CAD 100 per failure; gross negligence penalties and criminal prosecution are possible for repeated or deliberate non-filing; partner allocation claims may be denied or delayed.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory independent statutory audit is imposed on a Quebec limited partnership (société en commandite) by the Act respecting legal publicity or the Civil Code of Québec. An audit may become mandatory if required by the partnership agreement, by lenders or investors, if the LP becomes a reporting issuer under securities law, or if CRA issues a formal audit demand on partner allocations.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP applicable to private enterprises, specifically Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) or IFRS where required by the partnership agreement or creditor covenant. Revenu Québec and CRA accept Canadian GAAP applied consistently.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The REQ annual declaration must confirm for each Quebec LP: registered office address, general partners, limited partners and capital contributions, and ultimate beneficial owner information. Transfers of limited partnership interests must be disclosed in the next REQ annual declaration filing window; changes to general partners, the partnership name, or the registered address must be reported immediately, not deferred to the annual cycle. Quebec's legal publicity regime does not create a stand-alone public UBO corporate register for LPs, but UBO attributes are embedded in the REQ central record.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited and General Partners with Capital Contributions
Register of Partnership Resolutions and Consents
Minute Book (fiscal and administrative records maintained per Income Tax Act record-keeping requirements)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150 - USD 450 per year for registered office or compliance agent services in Quebec, including annual declaration preparation
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,500 - USD 12,000 for a small to mid-size market-research partnership audited under Canadian GAAP

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Fiscally transparent regime: the Quebec Limited Partnership (LP) is not a taxpayer under ITA s. 96 and s. 750 of the Quebec Taxation Act (QTA); income is allocated to partners and taxed at partner level. For comparative context, a Quebec-resident corporate partner would face a combined statutory general corporate income tax rate of 26.5% (15% federal Part I general corporate rate + 11.5% Quebec corporate rate), while an individual Quebec-resident partner faces a combined top marginal rate of approximately 53.31%. A non-resident corporate partner earning Canadian-source business income through the LP is taxed at the 15% federal Part I rate plus 25% Part XIV branch tax Absent treaty relief, for an aggregate non-treaty effective burden of 36.25%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday applies to ISIC 7320 market-research platforms. Available incentives: (1) Federal SR&ED Investment Tax Credit of 37.73% refundable for a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) partner claiming its allocable share of eligible software/R&D expenditures incurred by the LP; (2) Quebec R&D tax credit on eligible salaries (maximum 32.3% NNTC, 14.4% for large corporations), claimable through the partner under QTA ss. 1029.5-1029.13; (3) If the sole partner is a CCPC, the first C$500,000 of allocable active business income may qualify for the reduced federal small business rate of 9% and the Quebec reduced rate of 3.2%, yielding a combined 12.2% on the business limit; (4) The LP itself pays no entity-level income or capital tax in Quebec.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal: T5013 Partnership Information Return (with T5013 Summary and T5013 slips) filed electronically via CRA 'Internet File Transfer' or through a third-party transmitter/EFILE; for partnerships with non-resident partners, filed under ITA ss. 96 and 229(d).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 5 months after the end of the partnership fiscal period (s. 229(d) ITA); for a calendar-year LP, due March 31 of the following year. The deadline runs from the fiscal year-end shown in Box 5 of the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal period end date (YYYY-MM-DD). Determines the statutory filing deadline and the partner allocation period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the LP is a multi-tiered structure, choose the fiscal period most recently ended before the reporting deadline; foreign partners must align their own T2/T1 reporting to this date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership Business Number (BN), a 9-digit account number; the LP must open a CRA 'LP' account for the BN even though it pays no tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident partner must hold its own BN for a Canadian T2/T1 filing; the LP must report the partner's BN in the T5013 partner slip field.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership type code (General Partnership, Limited Partnership, or Limited Liability Partnership). A Quebec LP files the 'Limited Partnership' code and jurisdiction of formation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The code confirms the entity is fiscally transparent; a non-resident partner cannot use this field to claim the partnership is a taxable entity or treaty-independent person.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of each partner's share of net business income (loss), taxable capital gains, and income from Canadian sources; the percentage used must reproduce the LP Agreement and applicable Quebec Civil Code rules on participation in profit and loss.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporate partner's allocable Canadian-source active business income must be separated from foreign-source amounts; the 'source jurisdiction' column must be populated to permit the partner's treaty relief and foreign tax credit analysis.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: ITA s. 162(7.1): C$25 per day for each day of delay up to 100 days (minimum C$250, maximum C$2,500) for the T5013 return; larger penalties apply to partnerships with more than 50 partners. CRA adds daily compound interest on unpaid partner tax at the prescribed rate (90-day Treasury bill + 2%), and under s. 238, a knowing failure to file is a criminal offense punishable by a fine of up to C$25,000 and imprisonment up to 12 months.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Revenu Québec: R-5013 (Sociétés de personnes) information return with RL-15 slips, filed through the 'Cliquez' business portal or via XML/GEN-IP transfer; registration of the LP's 'NEQ' and tax account is required before electronic filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 5 months after the end of the LP's fiscal year (s. 1009 QTA); for a December 31 year-end, due March 31. Non-resident partners must file their own Quebec TP-1/T2 returns within the same deadline if they derive income from a Quebec place of business.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec enterprise registration number (NEQ) and mailing address; confirm the LP is registered with the Registraire des entreprises under the Loi sur la publicité légale des entreprises.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners using a Quebec address for service must provide a 'demandeur non-résident' declaration; proofs of Quebec permanent establishment must be uploaded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Case 2 – code de société de personnes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Code describing the partnership type (limited, general, or co-ownership) and the commercial activity code (NAICS 541910 for market research and public opinion polling).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The code is required to compute the Quebec allocation (Quebec-place-of-business formula); the non-resident partner must apply the same code on its TP-1/T2 return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Case 4 – income breakdown (partners' names, INS/BN, addresses, and share of Quebec-source income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Each partner's name, social insurance number or business number, resident status, and share of income allocated to Quebec in dollars and percentage.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For each non-resident partner, indicate province/state of residence and, if the partner claims a treaty exemption, attach the certificate of residence (Revenu Québec accepts the CRA/TRC or a government-issued certificate).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: QTA s. 1088: C$25 per day of arrears (min C$250, max C$2,500) for the R-5013; RL-15 slip penalties run up to C$25 daily per missing slip; daily compound interest is charged on unpaid balances by Revenu Québec at its prescribed rate; a false or misleading declaration is prosecutable under s. 1763 QTA with fines and imprisonment up to 24 months.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporate Income Tax Return (for each partner corporation, including the non-resident corporate general partner deemed to carry on business through the LP's place of business); filed via CRA's 'Internet File Transfer' or commercial software (EFILE).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (per partner corporation's own fiscal year)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The T2 return is due within 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end; the tax balance is due within 2 months after year-end for a Canadian-controlled private corporation and within 3 months for other corporations, and non-resident corporations with no other Canadian establishment pay instalments under s. 157 of the ITA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Inclusion of the partner's share of the LP's business income (or loss) under s. 96; aggregate of the partnership's 'gröss revenue' and expense lines must be reproduced.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporate partner only includes the share attributable to the LP's Canadian permanent establishment; foreign-source allocations are excluded from Canadian Part I taxation but remain subject to the partner's residency rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 21 – Partnership Income (for the corporate partner)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciling accounting net income to tax allocation: allocation percentage, guaranteed payments, and any section 96(2.1) adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the T5013 and the R-5013 for the LP; a treaty relief schedule (Schedule 21 and Form T2207) is required if the partner seeks reduction of Part I or Part XIV taxes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part I – Tax Payable and Part XIV – Branch Tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total federal Part I on taxable income; if the return is for a non-resident corporation, a further schedule to compute the 25% branch tax under s. 219 (or the reduced treaty rate) on the after-tax Canadian business income not reinvested in Canada.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The branch tax base excludes remitted profits that were included in the partner's taxable Canadian income in prior years; claim a treaty reduction by filing a completed TRC and the appropriate schedule.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: ITA s. 162(1): 5% of the unpaid tax balance for a late-filed T2, plus 1% per month for up to 12 months; balance-due interest at the prescribed daily rate; s. 163(2) gross negligence penalty of 50% of the understated tax; deliberately false returns are prosecuted under s. 239 with fines of up to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Statutory Part XIII rate of 25% applies to 'dividends' paid by a Canadian-resident corporation to non-resident recipients (ITA s. 212(2)). Critical: a Quebec LP is fiscally transparent; distributions of profit to partners are NOT dividends and are NOT subject to Part XIII withholding. Instead, the non-resident partner is taxable directly under Part I on its allocated Canadian-source business income; a non-resident corporate partner is further subject to Part XIV branch tax of 25% on after-tax income (reducible under a tax treaty). Quebec does not impose a separate dividend withholding tax on partnership distributions to partners.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke the Canada-Quebec DTA (where the partner is resident in a treaty country such as the US, UK, France, or Mexico), the following administrative process applies: (1) the non-resident partner obtains a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from its home tax authority (e.g., IRS Form 6166 for US partners) valid for the year; (2) the partner delivers the TRC to the LP before any distribution; (3) the LP retains a copy in its books and reports the treaty-reduced allocation on T5013/R-5013; (4) if the LP or its Canadian withhold agent is required to withhold at 25%, the partner may file an NR301 or NR302 bypass/form with the payer to apply the reduced treaty rate in advance; (5) for non-resident corporate partners, a Part XIV treaty reduction is claimed on the T2 return by attaching Form T2207 and the TRC; (6) the partner files a T1 (individual) or T2 (corporation) to recover any over-withholding (refund statute-barred after three years under s. 164).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory federal Part XIII withholding on royalties and interest paid by a Canadian payer to a non-resident is 25% (ITA s. 212(1)(b),(c)); Quebec imposes its own parallel withholding at 25% on similar Quebec-source payments. Under the Canada-US treaty: interest paid to a US resident at arm's length is exempt from Canadian withholding (0%); interest not at arm's length is generally limited to 15% (or 10% where the recipient is a qualifying financial institution); royalties for patents, know-how, trademarks and market-research data are generally subject to 10% withholding (0% for certain copyright and computer-software royalties). For the platform's outbound subscription/licence fees paid to non-residents for use of survey software or consumer data, the source rules of ss. 212(1)(d) and 212(1.1) must be applied, and a TRC plus treaty declaration must accompany any reduced rate claim. Note: payments to foreign consumer panelists via PayPal Mass Payout/Wise are generally service fees falling outside Part XIII if the panelist has no Canadian permanent establishment; however, CRA treats consideration for 'advice, research or analysis of consumer behavior' as a royalty under treatys depending on the facts, so a TP and source characterization review is critical.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: ITA s. 237.1: Form T106 must be filed for any non-arm's length cross-border transaction if the aggregate value in a transaction category with one non-resident exceeds C$1,000,000 per fiscal year (single category threshold aggregated across all transactions with that person). CRA requires contemporaneous 'complete and accurate documentation' for those transactions; documentation must be prepared in English or French and delivered within 3 months of a written demand from CRA. Additionally, for the LP's multinational group (including a foreign parent or sister entities), Country-by-Country Reporting is mandatory only when the consolidated group revenue of the ultimate parent equals or exceeds the annual CbCR threshold (currently approximately C$757 million); a master file and local file are not statutorily separate filings in Canada, but CRA audits treat the T106, organizational charts, and TP policy as the effective master/local file substitute.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) applied in MENA jurisdictions do not operate in Canada. Instead, Canada applies: (1) the General Anti-Avoidance Rule of ITA s. 245 (mirrored by Quebec under ss. 1079.6 – 1079.9 QTA), which permits CRA to disregard any avoidance transaction lacking a bona fide commercial purpose and genuine economic substance; (2) the OECD/G20 BEPS aggressive tax planning disclosures and Multilateral Instrument Principal Purpose Test, which can deny treaty benefits to partnership structures created primarily to reduce withholding tax; and (3) the Quebec civil law doctrine under Book 8 of the Civil Code of Quebec (arts. 2236–2245) requiring that a limited partnership possess a real commercial business and that limited partners refrain from taking part in management. The LP must maintain in Quebec its own office, employees, customer contracts, payment infrastructure accounts (including PayPal/Wise settlement accounts), board decision-logic, and accounting records; otherwise CRA may disregard the partnership and allocate its income directly to the non-resident partners, invalidating the intended pass-through treatment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and False Declarations (Federal ITA s. 239(1), Quebec QTA s. 1763)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting or misallocating the income of a non-resident partner, inflating deductible expenses of the LP (e.g., fictitious royalties paid to a foreign sister entity for consumer-panel software), creating back-dated LP agreements, or using undisclosed nominee partners to conceal true beneficial ownership of the survey platform.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil: 50% gross-negligence penalty (ITA s. 163(2)) on the understated tax, plus daily compound interest and a separate 100% penalty for wilful evasion under s. 239(1) (civil increase of the tax sought to be evaded); criminal: on summary conviction a fine of 50%–100% of the evaded tax and imprisonment up to 2 years less a day; on indictment a fine of 100%–200% and imprisonment for up to 5 years. In Quebec, a false or deceptive return is punishable under s. 1763 QTA by fines up to double the tax sought to be avoided and imprisonment up to 24 months.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior officers of the corporate general partner who knowingly participated in the scheme are personally subject to criminal prosecution; the Criminal Code (other than the ITA) may additionally impose penalties for fraud to the use of an electronic platform with up to 14 years of imprisonment; civil fraud suits by minority partners or creditors can pierce the veil where the LP is a mere alter ego.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold Payroll, Part XIII, and Non-Resident Allocations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The LP pays crowdsourced survey respondents on a W-9-like basis without issuing T4A/RL-1 or without applying section 212(1)(d) royalty withholding on licensing-type payments to foreign panelists; or the LP omits the mandatory Quebec payroll source deductions (income tax, QPP, QPIP, health contribution) for platform employees; or it fails to withhold Part XIII on interest/royalty payments to a non-resident IP holder.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ITA s. 227(8): a 10% penalty on every amount that was required to be withheld but was not remitted, plus daily interest; failure to remit is a due-and-payable debt of the LP; criminal sanction under s. 227(9) of imprisonment of up to 2 years and fines where the failure was knowingly made; Revenu Québec applies the same scheme with additional penalties for late remittance of source deductions (s. 549 QTA).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the corporate general partner are personally, jointly, and severally liable under ITA s. 227.1 and QTA s. 1013.1 for the entire unremitted withholding, regardless of whether the LP is insolvent and even after the LP has been wound up; no insurance indemnity covers the director for such a debt; CRA routinely obtains writs of seizure and can initiate bankruptcy against the corporate general partner, forcing personal settlement by directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unregistered Money Service Business / AML Violations (Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the cross-border survey payout platform through PayPal Mass Payout and Wise while (i) holding, transferring, or transmitting funds in a manner that constitutes an MSB in Canada, (ii) failing to register with FINTRAC as an MSB, or (iii) failing to implement a Compliance Program, beneficial-ownership KYC, and suspicious-transaction reporting (STR) for payouts to hundreds of non-resident panelists.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties (AMPs) of up to C$1,000,000 for an individual and C$2,000,000 for a corporation for serious MSB violations; non-registration itself carries AMPs of up to C$250,000 (individual) and C$500,000 (entity) depending on the table; criminal violations for laundering proceeds or terror financing on conviction are punishable by imprisonment of up to 5 years and unlimited fines; FINTRAC may also enter a compliance agreement or freeze the platform's settlement accounts during audit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: S. 73.1 PCMLTFA: directors, officers, and partners who 'authorize, permit or acquiesce in' an MSB non-registration or AML failure are personally liable for the AMP; additionally, FINTRAC can seek injunctions, and criminal charges can result in travel bans/conditions attached to the sentence, preventing cross-border movement of directors during prosecution.
